newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Ciampi sees April CPI below two percent.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Ciampi sees April CPI below two percent.

text.p: Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday that he was convinced year-on-year inflation in Italy would fall to below two percent when preliminary April figures are released next week.

The March year-on-year level was 2.2 percent, the lowest since 1969, and preliminary consumer price data for April from 11 Italian cities are due to be released on April 21 and 22. ISTAT will publish final CPI data for April on May 6.
"Inflation is diminishing. We are expecting the data for April (next week) and I am convinced that we will go below two percent," Ciampi told reporters at the lower house of parliament.
Italian shares and bond futures have all firmed on expectations of an April year-on-year rate of 1.9 percent and a view that the fall could pave the way for the Bank of Italy to cut interest rates.

Traders also noted that Tuesday's February industrial production data, showing an unadjusted fall of 3.8 percent against a 6.4 percent decline in January, also boosted hopes for a rate cut. Ciampi called the figure "positive".
